item.description:

This event showcases both fine art and fine craft with works in apothecary, artisanal foods, ceramics, jewelry, wood, digital art, decorative and wearable fiber, furniture, glass, painting, 2D/3D mixed media and photography. item.title: Montclair Film Festival - Being Huemann — Sat Oct 17, 12:00 PM — The Wellmont Theater
item.description:
They wouldn’t take Judy Heumann’s phone calls, so she took their building. In 1977, a young disabled woman (Ruth Madeley) and a scrappy coalition of outsiders decide they’ve had enough. What begins as one impulsive act becomes the longest occupation of a federal building in American history, as hundreds spontaneously seize government offices and refuse to leave until the bureaucrat in their way (Mark Ruffalo) takes action. Bringing rebellion in all its forms to the hallowed halls, a movement’s accidental leaders struggle to find their path forward where none has ever been paved for them. Directed by Academy Award® winner Siân Heder (CODA) and based on true events, BEING HEUMANN is the revolutionary, irreverent, and deeply human story of the least likely people trying to pull off the impossible and change the lives of millions. This screening will feature multiple access options for our patrons. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: Cape May with Everything on it — Mon Oct 19, 7:30 AM — NJ
item.description: Join Louise Zemaitis for this three-day birding workshop exploring Cape May during the best time of year for massive bird fallouts! This is the time at Cape May that the local birders wait for; visiting crowds of keen birders have diminished, yet the most massive bird fallouts of the season commonly occur NOW! Flocks of sparrows, kinglets, bluebirds, American Robins and Hermit Thrushes throng the trees and meadows – and it is now that knowledgeable birders start to sift through the birds in the hope of something really special, since this week starts the season for vagrants in Cape May. It’s also a great time for big raptors like buteos and Golden Eagles, while large seabird flights pass Avalon and Cape May Point nearly every day. Most of the three days will be spent outdoors, learning directly from our field experiences and much of our time will most likely be spent at some of Cape May’s key migration locations. item.title: 🥾 Hemlock Falls and Orange Reservoir — Fri Oct 23, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! Let's Walk in South Mountain Reservation.
We'll start in the Tulip Springs parking lot off Cherry Ln in West Orange. We will follow the yellow trail and visit Hobble and **Hemlock Falls.** It will be a great time to view both falls if we get rain this week.
Next, we will retrace our steps to the Reservoir Trail and walk through the woods until we reach the connector and take it down the hill to the paved path. We'll make almost 1 full loop of the lake and then follow a short trail back to the Tulip Springs parking lot.
We will be walking about 3.4 miles on various surfaces in the woods and around the lake, so please wear sturdy shoes with good traction. **NO SNEAKERS, please.** Some will find a walking stick helpful especially when descending the connector trail.
**Don't forget to bring water**. We will be walking for 90-120 minutes
**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.** FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

item.title: Tech Toolbox: Setting Up Emergency Info — Tue Oct 27, 12:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Toolbox is a free hands-on workshop series focused on building real, practical digital skills. Each session zeroes in on a specific skill, program, or tool—from core computer skills and file management to navigating software and online platforms you use every day. Participants are encouraged to bring their own devices and follow along, so you'll leave each session having actually practiced what you learned.
All experience levels are welcome, and your instructor will be there to walk you through everything step by step. Sessions are free and open to the public.

item.title: Tech Talks: Staying Safe While Traveling — Tue Oct 27, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: Staying Safe While Traveling

item.title: Kill Goofy — Sat Oct 17, 8:00 AM — Grove Street Theater
item.description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. item.description: Do you ever find yourself questioning God’s role in your life…or your role in God’s universe? Maybe you relate to the Biblical Jacob, wrestling all night with a mysterious divine being, and clinging to him asking for blessing only after experiencing defeat? For this year’s annual retreat, October 23-25, the men of Union will explore the theme “Wrestling with God: Faith, Struggle, and the Blessing We Don’t Expect.” We will be guided on our journey by Reverend Jeff Mansfield, and we’ll be meeting in the comfortable surroundings of the Christ Center at Crossroads Camp located at 29 Pleasant Grove Rd., Port Murray, NJ 07865. The retreat is designed for reflection and recreation as we deepen our ties to one another both in themed conversation as well as through the camaraderie and fun of our informal time together.
